newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's Cullinan hotels to debut on JSE Monday.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's Cullinan hotels to debut on JSE Monday.

text.p: South African hotels firm Cullinan Hotel and Leisure Group said on Sunday that it will make its debut listing on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE) on Monday.

The move follows its 85 million rand purchase of travel agency Concorde Travel Holdings Ltd and is, in effect, a reverse listing. The new group, trading under the name CulTel, will have a market capitalisation of around 170 million rand.
Following the acquisition Cullinan will raise 71.6 million rand with a clawback offer that will issue 71.58 million new shares at 100 cents each. The offer to institutions has been fully subscribed.
The new group is forecasting earnings per share of 9.1 cents for 1997.

Cullinan managing director Martin Rodrigues said in a statement that the group plans to open four new hotels in the next two years with construction beginning on three of the new developments this month.
The firm currently has two hotels, both in Sandton near Johannesburg, and aims to become a national hotels group.
